To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) 18 out of 41 patients with the clinical diagnosis of HHT were found to carry a mutation in the ENG or ACVRL1 gene, 2) the novel ENG mutation c.1167delG was identified in a German patient with HHT and 3) the allele-specific PCR-SSP method is a fast, reliable, and cost effective method for genotyping of ENG/ACVRL1 mutations.
we have identified 15 different ENG and ACVLR1 mutations in 18 patients.

1) the ENG and ACVL1 genes are the major genes responsible for HHT, 2) mutation analysis in the ENG and ACVR1L genes is a valuable tool for the diagnosis of HHT, and 3) allele-specific PCR is a rapid and cost-effective method for the identification of mutations and SNPS in the ENG and ALVR1L genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular genetic analysis of HHT in German patients, the identification of new mutations in HHT genes, and the evaluation of a rapid genotyping method.
the identification of new mutations in the ENG and ACVL1 genes in patients with hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasis (HHT).
the molecular genetics of HHT and the establishment of a rapid genotyping method for HHT mutations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mutation analysis of ENG and ACVLR1 genes is useful for diagnosis, genetic counselling and prenatal testing.
mutation analysis for the ENG gene should be performed in all patients with the suspected clinical diagnosis of HHT.
the ENG gene is the most important genetic cause in patients with HHT, whereas the ACVRL gene is a less frequent cause of the disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mutation analysis for the ENG gene in German HHT patients is of high diagnostic value.
the mutation analysis in ENG and ACVL1 genes is an important tool to confirm the clinical diagnosis of HHT and to identify the genetic cause of the disorder.
the allele-specific PCR technique is a fast, reliable, and cost-effective method for the genotyping of mutations in ENG and ACVL1 in HHT patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the allele-specific PCR technique is a rapid, cost-effective and highly accurate alternative to direct sequencing.
rapid genotyping of ENG and ALK1 mutations and SNPs in the ENG and ALK-1 genes is feasible using allele-specific PCR-SSP methods.
rapid genotyping of ENG and ACVLR1 gene mutations in HHT patients is possible by PCR-SSP.
